relations.rationale: Booking a hall has no bearing on relative ages of Milo and Otto.
Jude showing up last is consistent with and slightly supports the idea he was rushing and out of breath.
Arriving last doesn't determine whether Jude was still talking about the seminar.
Arrival order has no bearing on relative height claims.
Being out of breath from rushing after a seminar supports that Jude would still be talking about that seminar.
Being out of breath from a late seminar supports the idea that an argument ran past its scheduled time, explaining the lateness.
Being out of breath from rushing has no bearing on height comparisons.
Jude's breathlessness from rushing is unrelated to the club's future meeting plans.
Milo having already picked seats near the window supports him then arranging chairs for visibility of the display.
Milo's seat choice is unrelated to Noor's book selection.
Seating choice is unrelated to the club's agreement on a future meeting.
Milo arranging chairs is unrelated to whether Otto is in Jude's class.
Otto and Kira being in the same class supports their habit of walking together after lectures.
Otto being in the same class as Kira is consistent with and supports Kira being in the same class as Jude only if Otto and Jude share class, but this is about Kira-Jude not directly implied.

If Otto is in the same class as Kira, and Kira could be in a different class than Jude, this doesn't determine Otto's relation to Jude directly, but combined with other facts it's ambiguous when judged alone.
Class membership has no bearing on height comparisons.
Otto and Kira's walking habit is unrelated to the club's meeting schedule.
Noor choosing a mystery novel supports Milo's approving nod at the suggestion.
Choosing a novel is unrelated to height comparisons.
Noor's book choice supports the club's plan to meet after new books arrive and are read.
